MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  JUNE 20, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A special meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:02 p.m. at the Ernie Howlett Park, 25851 Hawthorne Boulevard,
  Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR BAIN.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR BAIN led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Persichina,  Pope,  Ciarolla,  Holdsworth
  McCormick, and Bain

  Commissioners Absent:  Johnson

  City Staff Present:  Maintenance Superintendent Mike Goldsmith
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 15,
  2023

  COMMISSIONER POPE noted a minor grammatical correction on one of her
  statements in item 7C in the draft minutes of May 15, 2023.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR
  MCCORMICK to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  MAY 15, 2023, with the correction presented by COMMISSIONER POPE.

  There being no objection, VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

  6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
JUNE 20, 2023
   NONE.

  7.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT ROUTE CHANGE EFFECTIVE JULY 31, 2023 (VERBAL
  REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas gave a brief overview of the Waste Management route change.
  She noted that Waste Management and the City would be doing outreach to their
  customers.

  CHAIR BAIN asked if anyone had received any notifications regarding their specific
  neighborhoods. Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the notices may not have been
  sent yet.

  B.  PLANNING COMMISSION VACANCY (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the current vacancy on the City’s
  Planning Commission.

  C.  FOUNDERS PARK UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief update of the bidding process regarding the
  development of Founders Park. She stated that the two bids received for the project
  were over the engineer’s estimate for the project. She noted that Staff would
  recommend rejecting the current bids at the next City Council meeting and propose
  the project be re-bid with modifications made to the project’s irrigation and
  landscaping costs.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that typically the City does accept the lowest bid on
  projects, in response to COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA.

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the City is proposing modifications to the irrigation
  and sizes of plants and other options to lower costs, in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK stated that the former chairman of the Rolling Hills
  Country Club came to one of the Commission meetings a few years ago and stated
  that they would assist in covering some of the cost of the irrigation of the park project
  when they were utilizing the lot for parking during their construction of the country
  club. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that she would speak to the Public Works Director
  regarding the matter.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
JUNE 20, 2023
   CHAIR BAIN asked if the Commission would be able to review the modifications
  prior to the new bid process. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that it would continue to
  be reviewed by the City Council.

  D.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas shared that City Manager Greg Grammer is conducting a
  social media video series called City Manager in the Park.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the first video looked great and that he did a
  great job.

  CHAIR BAIN stated that she gave him some feedback and he was very responsive
  to it.

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that Silver Spur Park looks great.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked about the progress of the removal of the poison
  oak at the George F. Canyon Nature Preserve. Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  that it is in progress and that he is hoping Maintenance staff would be able to have
  it all removed in a couple of weeks.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH asked about the fence line next to the horse
  property at Rockbluff Park and if it was a private fence or a City fence.
  Superintendent Goldsmith stated that he is aware of the area and is researching
  who owns the fence.

  CHAIR BAIN stated that Highridge Park looks great and that the plants in the turf
  removal project are looking great as well.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if Staff has been able to go to Highridge Park to
  look into the dogs off leash problem on Thursdays. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that
  she has made a request to Code Enforcement to address the issue and that they
  are working on it. She noted that Code also reached out to Animal Control to assist
  in patrolling the park during that time. CHAIR BAIN stated that there may be a need
  to add more signage around the pathways along the grass field areas of the park.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
JUNE 20, 2023
   9.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF APRIL 11, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF APRIL 25, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  10.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  REVISED COMMITTEE/SUBCOMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  B.  HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE UPATE

  C.  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH PAGEANTRY PRODUCTIONS

  D.  PUBLIC PARK OUTREACH

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of all the future agenda items.

  11.  PARK TOURS

  A.  ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  CHAIR BAIN offered some more words of encouragement regarding the initial Ernie
  Howlett Park City Manager in the Park video and that it was very well done.

  **AT THIS POINT THE COMMISSION CONDUCTED A PARK TOUR OF ERNIE
  HOWLETT PARK**

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH stated that he has noticed a group setting up a
  volleyball net on the outfield area of the baseball fields and if there were any plans
  on updating or renovating the sand volleyball area in the park. He also stated that
  the groups he has spoken to informed him that it is not a good playing surface
  currently and has a lot of animal waste in the sand as well. Supervisor Pinuelas
  stated that Staff is currently reviewing some ideas regarding that area that include
  possibly renovating the area for a more productive volleyball playing area or
  changing the area completely to add a shaded picnic structure in the park.
  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that the main group that plays volleyball in
  the grass was the group that requested that the City install the sand volleyball court
  but that they can’t currently play on a sand surface anymore due to their age.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
JUNE 20, 2023
   CHAIR BAIN asked if Staff is currently tracking the pickleball play at the tennis
  courts. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that although Staff is not keeping actual counts
  that there has been an increase in pickleball play on the overlayed courts.

  Superintendent Goldsmith noted that Staff has provided some roll away trash cans
  for Silver Spur Little League to dispose of some of their oversized trash, but that
  they have not utilized the cans to dispose of the current trash as requested by Staff.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the area along the broken fence line next to
  the little league snack shed that has been marked with caution tape. Superintendent
  Goldsmith noted that a large tree fell down and Staff has been working on removal
  of the debris and fixing up the area.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noticed that the extra sod that Silver Spur Little
  League had brought for field maintenance and had left along the field line since
  January had been thrown into that closed off area. Superintendent Goldsmith stated
  that he would look into the matter as his crew was cleaning up the area recently
  and would work on removing it.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA offered words of encouragement to
  Superintendent Goldsmith about his work in reducing the amount of gopher holes
  in the baseball fields at the park. He stated that some of the other local baseball
  fields in surrounding cities are so inundated with gopher holes.

  COMMISSIONER POPE noticed two large crates next to the batting cage and shed
  area adjacent to Field B and asked what they were. Superintendent Goldsmith
  stated that it was a new scoreboard that was approved for Silver Spur Little League
  to install on top of the batting cage as well as the removal and installation of a new
  shed. Staff noted that Little League had arranged for a volunteer to assist in the
  installation of the new scoreboard, but notified Staff that the volunteer was no longer
  available, in response to COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked about the shed behind the home plate area
  of Field B as it was unlocked. COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH stated that it was
  AYSO’s shed as it had most of their field materials inside. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA stated that it was approved initially for Silver Spur Little League use.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff would notify both groups to see who has been
  using the shed to ensure that the shed is consistently locked.

  CHAIR BAIN asked about a large dirt and grass mound area behind the Field B
  third base dugout. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that when Little League does
  field maintenance, they dump dirt and grass in random locations. COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA stated that it is not supposed to be there and should be removed and

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
JUNE 20, 2023
   believes staff has already notified the league president. Supervisor Pinuelas
  confirmed that Staff has notified the league president to remove that item.

  Supervisor Pinuelas informed the Commission that AYSO would not be utilizing the
  fields for their 2023 soccer season but would return in 2024. She stated that Staff
  is planning to shut down the fields in August for an enhanced field maintenance and
  rest period to last until the end of December. Superintendent Goldsmith stated that
  Maintenance staff is going to try to fill an area in Field B that has sunken due to
  some settling over time that has occurred and also due to the most recent weather.

  Coordinator Morrow informed the Commission of a recent incident with the Junior
  League and their attempt to do some field modifications. He informed the
  Commission that they dumped two truckloads of brick dust on the infield without
  any notification to Staff. He stated that Staff notified a representative of the league
  and the representative informed Staff that they wanted to improve the infield with
  better brick dust and some infield edging. He stated that they also informed Staff
  that they wanted to make modifications to the field and install new 90ft base posts
  and reshape the pitching mound to include a 60ft pitching rubber. Staff then reached
  out to the acting president of Junior League to inform him that the City approved
  the routine maintenance of the infield, but did not approve the pitching mound and
  base path modifications. Coordinator Morrow stated that the Junior League
  proceeded with the unapproved modifications, having removed the 80ft base posts
  and installed the 90ft base posts. Upon realizing that this action had occurred Staff
  removed the 90ft base posts, notified the acting president on the City’s action, and
  reiterated that no further maintenance could be completed by Junior League without
  City approval.

  Supervisor Pinuelas added that Staff has notified Junior League on multiple
  occasions over the past three months of the need to repaint their shed after damage
  caused by a small fire which was accidentally set by one of their volunteers. She
  stated that Staff will now have to repaint the shed and invoice the league due to
  their inaction after repeated communication by the City.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA informed the group that Junior League does have
  a 60x90 field available at George Allen Field in Palos Verdes Estates for them to
  use if they desire those dimensions.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if Junior League is part of Silver Spur Little League.
  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH stated that Junior League was founded by
  Silver Spur and is still chartered by Silver Spur under Little League International but
  has been allowed to run autonomously due to financial concerns by Silver Spur
  when the league launched. He noted that Silver Spur is the chartering member, but
  Junior League does have its own independent board. COMMISSIONER POPE
  asked if this meant that the City has a separate agreement with Junior League.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
JUNE 20, 2023
   Supervisor Pinuelas confirmed that the City does have a separate one-year
  agreement with Junior League, but they have not been fully compliant with all the
  terms of that agreement recently and Staff is hoping to be able to communicate with
  them to address some of these issues in accordance with the new sports filed usage
  policy. Coordinator Morrow stated that it appears that Junior League will have new
  leadership for the next season and that Staff is planning to meet with them to go
  over the agreement and the new sports field policy.

  In response to CHAIR BAIN, Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff has informed the
  leagues that the City needs to be notified prior to these major improvements due to
  safety concerns including trucks going onto the field and possible damage to the
  fields and irrigation. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that unless the City
  takes ownership of the fields and sets maintenance rules it will continue to be
  difficult to ensure that these issues don’t continue to happen. Supervisor Pinuelas
  reiterated that Staff will continue to try and communicate with league
  representatives to work towards a win-win solution.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the Remember the Music Festival is returning this
  year. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that they have reached out but that their initial date
  did not end up working and that Staff have not heard back from them regarding a
  new date.

  As the Commission walked towards the barn and horse arena area of the park,
  CHAIR BAIN asked about the siding damage to the top of the barn. Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated that he is aware of the damage but is not sure how it occurred.
  He noted that due to the settlement of the ground, the front side of the barn is
  shorter than the back side of the barn. He also stated that the barn is still structurally
  sound.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the trees in front of the picnic table along the trail
  behind the barn could be trimmed. Superintendent Goldsmith affirmed, stating that
  the plan is to remove some due to the trees dying.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK asked if there were any requests for film permits.
  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that it didn’t seem like there were many requests.

  VICE CHAIR MCCORMICK stated that there seemed to be a need for a crosswalk
  or signage near the newly installed fitness equipment along the entrance driveway
  to the park as he has noticed kids crossing from the playground and grass area
  through the street to get to the fitness equipment.

  As the Commission walked towards the tennis courts, COMMISSIONER POPE
  asked if the pickleball overlay lines on the tennis courts were permanent. Supervisor

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
JUNE 20, 2023
   Pinuelas stated that the pickleball lines are permanent but that the nets were
  portable.

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH asked if there have been any complaints
  regarding pickleball from neighboring residents. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that
  there have not been complaints from the residents surrounding the park. She stated
  that a few complaints have come from tennis players or even other pickleball
  players regarding pickleball groups monopolizing the courts.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR BAIN ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 7:05 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JULY 17, 2023, AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH
  WILL BE HELD AT HIGHRIDGE PARK.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________
  Matt Morrow  Judy Bain
  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  8
JUNE 20, 2023
